description:
Project Title: Abandoned, But Not Forgotten — Interplanetary Heritage (1950–2026)
About Us & Vision: We are a passionate space-tech initiative dedicated to transforming how humanity perceives extraterrestrial hardware. Instead of viewing leftover lunar and Martian modules, landers, and rovers as mere "debris," we treat them as our solar system’s first archaeological artifacts and sacred interplanetary heritage.
What We Are Building: An immersive 3D interactive web.
summary: An interactive 3D web application that reimagines NASA's discarded lunar and Martian hardware as humanity's first extraterrestrial archaeological heritage. Featuring dual Moon and Mars globes, precise mission coordinates, and a 1950–2026 chronological timeline, it transforms space exploration history into an engaging storytelling experience.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?
"Abandoned, but not Forgotten" is an interactive 3D web application archiving extraterrestrial hardware on the Moon and Mars from 1950 to 2026. Built with Three.js, it features dual 3D globes, timelines, coordinate telemetry, and material wear tracking.
2. What benefits does it have?
It serves as an educational registry and digital heritage archive for students and researchers. It bridges space exploration history with modern web tech, providing open access to verified NASA Planetary Data System records.
3. What is the intended impact of the project?
The impact is raising global awareness about off-world cultural heritage. It helps researchers and upcoming missions, like NASA's Artemis program, prevent accidental disturbances or damage to historic lunar and Martian landing sites.
4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?
Developed using HTML5, Tailwind CSS, and JavaScript. Core 3D rendering uses Three.js and OrbitControls. It also integrates Web Audio API, Web Speech API for narration, and official landing coordinates from NASA PDS records.
5. How is your project creative?
It reframes abandoned spacecraft not as space debris, but as precious interplanetary archaeological heritage. By combining interactive dual 3D globes, material decay telemetry, and time-travel elements, it offers a unique browser storytelling format.
6. What factors did your team consider?
Key factors include accurate historical telemetry, scientific grounding via NASA data, and environmental wear factors like solar UV. Emphasis was placed on responsive mobile performance, intuitive UI design, and cross-browser compatibility without heavy installations.
